books.section: Portugal and Spain Lead the Way
Topic 1.3 European exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Spain wanted to send an army to conquer India before Portugal's ships arrived there
options.misconception: Spain sought a route to Asian trade, not an army to conquer India; Portugal reached India first.

options.text: Spain wanted to find a shorter route to the gold mines of West Africa
options.misconception: Puts the goal in the wrong ocean; West African gold was Portugal's trade, and Columbus sailed west for Asia.

options.text: Spain wanted to prove that the earth was flat and the ocean ended at the horizon
options.misconception: Repeats a myth; educated Europeans knew the earth was round, and Columbus argued about its size, not its shape.

options.text: Spain wanted its own sea route to Asia because Portugal's route around Africa belonged to Portugal

rationales.general:
1. Picture the locked door. Background from the books: Portugal owned the only sea route to India, built over decades around Africa, and Spain had no key.
2. Ask what Spain lacked. Any route of its own to Asian spices and silk.
3. Meet the gamble. Columbus offered a westward shortcut across the Atlantic, based on a wrong guess about the earth's size.
4. Check the motive. Spain funded the voyage to get its own road, not to conquer India or prove the earth flat.
Remember: when a rival owns the only road, the second power bets on a new one.
rationales.D: Portugal owned the African route, so Spain needed a different way to Asian trade. Columbus offered a western shortcut, and Spain funded the bet.
rationales.A: Spain never sent an army to conquer India, and Portugal reached India first in 1498. The goal was a trade route, not a conquest.
rationales.B: West African gold was Portugal's trade, and Columbus sailed west across the Atlantic for Asia. The goal was a new route east, not African gold.
rationales.C: Educated Europeans knew the earth was round. Columbus argued the earth was smaller than it is, not that it was flat.

stem: Portuguese ships reached India by sea in 1498, but Spain had no route of its own to Asia. Which of the following best explains why Spain then funded Columbus's westward voyage?

stimulus.source_note: Engraving by Frans Huys after Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 16th century, public domain (Metropolitan Museum of Art, CC0); text summarizes the Portuguese voyages down the African coast.
stimulus.text: Portuguese caravels crept down the African coast across the 1400s, each voyage pushing farther in search of a sea route to the spice markets of Asia. The engraving shows sailing ships of the 1500s with large triangular lateen sails, the sails that let caravels sail against the wind.
